definitions.explanation: The judge who leads and presides over court proceedings.

examples.japanese: {裁判長|さいばんちょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{判決|はんけつ}→判決：05906_hanketsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}い{渡|わた}した→言い渡す：07002_iiwatasu⟧。
examples.english: The presiding judge delivered the verdict.

examples.japanese: {裁判長|さいばんちょう}、⟦{異議|いぎ}→異議：13552_igi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Your Honor, I have an objection.

examples.japanese: {裁判長|さいばんちょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{開廷|かいてい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{宣言|せんげん}した→宣言する：21680_sengensuru⟧。
examples.english: The presiding judge declared the court in session.

notes:
{裁判長|さいばんちょう} is the presiding judge who leads court proceedings. Composed of ⟦{裁判|さいばん}→裁判：02773_saiban⟧ (trial, judgment) + {長|ちょう} (chief, head).

FUNCTIONS:
The {裁判長|さいばんちょう} manages the trial, maintains courtroom order, questions witnesses, and delivers the verdict. In Japan's three-judge panel system ({合議制|ごうぎせい}), the {裁判長|さいばんちょう} leads the other two judges.

USAGE:
In court, lawyers address the judge as {裁判長|さいばんちょう} ("Your Honor"). The phrase {裁判長|さいばんちょう}、⟦{異議|いぎ}→異議：13552_igi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧ ("Your Honor, I object") is well-known from courtroom dramas.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{裁判官|さいばんかん}→裁判官：09562_saibankan⟧: judge (general term for any judge)
- ⟦{判事|はんじ}→判事：00088_hanji⟧: judge (formal title in the court system)
- ⟦{裁判所|さいばんしょ}→裁判所：09665_saibansho⟧: court, courthouse
- ⟦{検察官|けんさつかん}→検察官：09664_kensatsukan⟧: prosecutor
- ⟦{弁護士|べんごし}→弁護士：03150_bengoshi⟧: lawyer, attorney
